nodes.label: WisDOT I-39/90/94 Corridor Study Logo Screenshot
nodes.description: Screenshot of the official Wisconsin Department of Transportation branding badge for the I-39/90/94 Corridor Study. A hexagonal emblem on a navy chevron-pattern background: illustrated highway scene with sandstone bluffs, pine trees, river and sky; three red/blue interstate shields (39, 90, 94); a green banner reading CORRIDOR STUDY; the tagline COMMERCE - SAFETY - TOURISM; and the circular WisDOT seal on the roadway. Stored in assets/images, likely as a blog/news illustration for Sprecher East residents about the regional highway study.
nodes.norm_label: wisdot i-39/90/94 corridor study logo screenshot

nodes.label: Wisconsin Department of Transportation (WisDOT)

nodes.label: Interstate 39/90/94 Corridor
nodes.description: The concurrent interstate highway segment represented by the three shields (I-39, I-90, I-94) in the emblem; the subject of the study.

nodes.label: Commerce, Safety, Tourism (Study Goals)
nodes.description: The three stated pillars printed on the badge that frame why the corridor study exists: supporting freight/commerce, improving traffic safety, and serving tourism travel to northern Wisconsin destinations.
nodes.rationale: The tagline communicates the study's justification to the public: the corridor is an economic, safety and tourism artery, so improvements are framed around those three benefits.

nodes.label: I-39/90/94 Corridor Study
nodes.description: Wisconsin DOT planning study of the Interstate 39/90/94 corridor (the shared interstate segment running through Madison's east side toward the Wisconsin Dells), covering future capacity, interchange and safety improvements.
nodes.rationale: Relevant to the Sprecher East website because the neighborhood sits on Madison's far east side adjacent to the I-39/90/94 corridor; study outcomes affect local traffic, noise, access and development (inferred from asset placement in a neighborhood news site).

nodes.label: Seed image post3 (abstract dark concentric amber arcs)
nodes.description: 16:9 abstract 3D render on a near-black / very dark navy background. Two large glossy concentric curved bands sweep from the lower-left toward the upper-right, each edge rim-lit with a warm amber/gold glow; the widest amber-lit arc dominates the right third of the frame and a tighter fold curls in at the lower-left. In this repo the resulting media doc (image3) is no longer a blog hero at all; it is wired into the About page as mapImage, while post 3's hero uses image1Doc instead. nodes.label: Local-first seed image fallback pattern
nodes.description: Seed media loading pattern: try loadLocalImage(neighborhood photo) first, catch and fall back to fetchFileByURL(Payload template stock webp). image-post1.webp is the fallback for the first media doc (image1, alt text: Sprecher East neighborhood community).
nodes.rationale: Real neighborhood photos are the desired content, but they may be absent in CI or a fresh clone; the upstream template image guarantees a deterministic, always-available placeholder so the seed and static build (generateStaticParams) do not break.

nodes.label: Payload Website Template stock seed image
nodes.description: The set of placeholder .webp images (image-post1/2/3, image-hero1) that ship with the Payload CMS v3 Website Template seed and are referenced by canonical raw.githubusercontent.com URLs.
nodes.norm_label: payload website template stock seed image
nodes.rationale: The template ships abstract stock art so the demo site renders with hero images out of the box. Sprecher East replaced the content in PR #34 but retained the remote URLs as a fallback so the seed never fails on a fresh checkout without local photos (explicit fallback rather than silently missing media).

nodes.label: Payload Website Template stock hero asset
nodes.description: Vestigial asset inherited from the Payload CMS Website Template (templates/website/src/endpoints/seed/image-hero1.webp). The Sprecher East seed script does not read the checked-in copy; it loads assets/images/photo.jpeg first and, on failure, fetches this same filename from raw.githubusercontent.com.
nodes.norm_label: payload website template stock hero asset
nodes.rationale: Sprint 2 content migration replaced template placeholders with Sprecher East content, but the binary template images stayed in the repo. The seed's remote fallback URL means the local webp is effectively dead weight and a candidate for removal or for being used as the local fallback instead of a network fetch.

nodes.label: About page map image fallback mismatch
nodes.description: When assets/images/East_Madison_NAs.png is absent (CI, fresh clone), the seed uploads this abstract stock render under the alt text 'East Madison neighborhood associations map' and the About page renders it in its map media block.
nodes.norm_label: about page map image fallback mismatch
nodes.rationale: The local-first / remote-fallback chain keeps seeding deterministic and non-failing, which is the intended trade-off, but for image3 the fallback silently swaps a factual neighborhood map for decorative template art while keeping the map alt text. That conflicts with the project's truth-over-speed and accessibility rules (alt text must describe the image) and is a signal that the fallback for this slot should either be a neutral placeholder with matching alt text or the About page should omit the map block when the real asset is missing.

nodes.label: Payload Website Template Placeholder Seed Image
nodes.norm_label: payload website template placeholder seed image
nodes.rationale: The Payload CMS Website Template ships four generic abstract renders as demo post/hero images so a fresh install has visual content. Sprecher East kept the files in src/endpoints/seed/ after adopting the template (PR #33/#34 content migration) but repointed the seed to real neighborhood photos in assets/images/; the abstract render survives only as the remote fallback so seeding never fails on a machine (e.g. CI) that lacks the local photos. Note: the Media alt text applied to this slot (image-2.ts: 'Neighborhood scenery in the Sprecher East area') describes a photo, so when the fallback fires the alt text does not match the abstract render actually uploaded.

nodes.label: Dark backdrop for hero text legibility
nodes.norm_label: dark backdrop for hero text legibility
nodes.rationale: The image is almost entirely low-luminance navy/black, so white hero headline and CTA text placed over it meets contrast requirements without a heavy gradient scrim. This is the property the template relies on for its HighImpact hero; a bright neighborhood photo substituted in its place needs the project's scrim utilities (bottom-up gradient or hero-text-readable shadow stack) to keep the same legibility.

nodes.label: Seed hero image local-first / remote-fallback loading
nodes.norm_label: seed hero image local-first / remote-fallback loading
nodes.rationale: The seed tries a real neighborhood photo from assets/images (two candidate paths via loadLocalImage) and only falls back to the upstream template's image-hero1.webp over HTTP. This lets seeding succeed in CI and fresh clones that lack the gitignored local photo set, while production/dev seeds with real Sprecher East imagery. Trade-off: the fallback depends on network access to GitHub and on the upstream template keeping that path stable.

nodes.label: Local-First Seed Image Loading with Remote Template Fallback
nodes.norm_label: local-first seed image loading with remote template fallback
nodes.rationale: Seeding uses loadLocalImage(filename).catch(() => fetchFileByURL(payloadTemplateRawUrl)) for each of the four media slots. Real Sprecher East imagery (assets/images/) wins when present, keeping seeded content on-brand; the Payload template's raw.githubusercontent.com copies of image-post1/2/3.webp and image-hero1.webp guarantee the seed still completes in CI or a fresh clone where those photos are absent. The trade-off is a network dependency on the upstream Payload repo and off-brand abstract imagery whenever the fallback is taken.

nodes.label: SITE_TIMEZONE / timezone utility

nodes.label: Tree Trunk and Canopy Photo (image-asset.jpeg)

The generic filename 'image-asset.jpeg' is the naming convention Squarespace uses for exported images, suggesting this was carried over from a previous site (AMBIGUOUS). nodes.label: Content Moderation Rules
nodes.rationale: Auto-flag comments with links (spam) and profanity/slurs; suggest diplomatic auto-responses; never delete without admin review — flag and hide instead.

nodes.label: Brand Voice and Tone
nodes.rationale: Warm and welcoming, honest and transparent (AI-assisted and unofficial, said openly), practical, inclusive, optimistic but grounded.

nodes.label: Comment Moderation Guidelines
nodes.rationale: Welcome disagreement but require respect; flag (do not delete) attacks, discrimination, misinformation, spam; respond diplomatically — acknowledge, redirect to facts, invite dialogue, never match anger.

nodes.label: Content Quality Standards
nodes.rationale: Every article needs a purpose, sourced claims, a specific benefit-oriented headline, a compelling excerpt, licensed self-hosted photos, and consistent categorization.

nodes.label: AI Transparency Disclosure
nodes.rationale: Prominent (footer/about/dedicated page), clear and specific about what AI does (content drafting, code generation, data analysis), clear about human volunteer oversight, and not apologetic — AI assistance is a feature, not a flaw.

nodes.label: Data Minimization
nodes.rationale: Collect only what is needed; usernames over real names; no phone numbers; cookieless analytics; delete inactive accounts with notice.

nodes.label: Unofficial Grassroots Status (not 501(c)(3))
nodes.rationale: Sprecher East is not a registered nonprofit or government entity, is run by volunteers with no formal liability protection, is AI-assisted, and collects minimal user data — this shapes every legal document.

nodes.label: Sprecher East Brand Name Rule
nodes.rationale: Always use the brand name "Sprecher East" — never "SENA". The project is an unofficial grassroots initiative and must always be transparent about AI assistance.

nodes.label: BoardMembers Collection
nodes.rationale: Basic fields, functional.

nodes.label: src/components/ (Shared UI)
nodes.rationale: Shared UI (UI primitives, Link, RichText, Media) with no strict layer boundaries.

nodes.label: Contact Form + /api/contact route
nodes.rationale: ContactForm.tsx is a client component posting to /api/contact/route.ts which only logs to console; email delivery still to be wired.

nodes.norm_label: src/lib/data.ts data layer (json fallback or sanity)

nodes.label: EventCard.tsx (legacy)
nodes.rationale: Compact + full-detail variants.

nodes.label: Formspree option for contact email

nodes.rationale: events.json (2 seeded I-39/90/94 hearing events), posts.json, board.json (4 placeholder slots), site.json — lets the site run with no CMS account.

nodes.label: Poppins via next/font/google

nodes.label: PostCard.tsx (legacy)

nodes.label: Resend option for contact email
nodes.rationale: Developer-friendly option with a generous free tier; add resend.emails.send() to route.ts.

nodes.label: Sanity v3 CMS (superseded)
nodes.rationale: Chosen for its React-based Studio embedded at /studio, Git-friendliness and free tier; later replaced by Payload CMS.

nodes.label: (site)/layout.tsx wrapping Nav + Footer
nodes.rationale: Solves nav/footer duplication: a single layout wraps all public pages so one change updates everywhere.

nodes.label: Vercel Hosting (original recommendation)
nodes.rationale: Recommended because it is made by the Next.js team, has a free tier and auto-deploys from GitHub; the project instead went live on a Hostinger VPS.

nodes.label: CodeRabbit Review Configuration
nodes.rationale: Chill review profile, high-level summary on, poem off, review status shown, auto-reply chat enabled; .github/** reviewed for security implications.

nodes.label: Project Handoff (Sanity-era, 2026-02-19)
nodes.rationale: Legacy handoff describing the Next.js + Tailwind + Sanity v3 build before the migration to Payload CMS; old static HTML files remained in root but were ignored by Next.js routing.

nodes.label: Layered Component Import Rules (ui -> features -> sections -> layout)
nodes.norm_label: layered component import rules (ui -> features -> sections -> layout)
nodes.rationale: Level 1 ui/ primitives are pure presentational and domain-agnostic; Level 2 features/ may import ui/ only; Level 3 sections/ may import ui/ and features/; layout/ (Nav, Footer, UserMenu) imports ui/ only; src/lib must not import components/. These paths mirror the pre-Payload (Sanity-era) structure and conflict with CLAUDE.md, which states src/components/ has no strict layer boundaries.

nodes.label: Client/Server Component Split
nodes.rationale: Nav is use client (mobile menu state), ContactForm is use client (form state), all pages are Server Components for data fetching.

nodes.label: WCAG 2.1 AA Accessibility Standard
nodes.rationale: Meaningful alt text, keyboard access, visible focus, aria labels on icon-only buttons, 4.5:1 / 3:1 contrast, skip navigation link.

nodes.label: Frontend Performance Rules
nodes.rationale: next/image with dimensions and lazy loading, dynamic imports for heavy components, prefer server components, check bundle size before adding deps.

nodes.label: ADA / WCAG 2.1 AA Compliance
nodes.rationale: All public pages must meet WCAG 2.1 AA; audit with axe-core or pa11y; document compliance status and known issues.

nodes.label: Alt Text Standards
nodes.rationale: Describe the image (no "image of"), contextual, under 125 chars, include location; empty alt for decorative; attribution goes in captions never alt text.

nodes.label: DJI Drone Photo Pipeline (RAW -> Web)
nodes.rationale: Convert DNG to JPEG/WebP, resize to 2400px max, quality 80-85%, strip EXIF GPS for privacy, rename for web.

nodes.label: Focal Point Support
nodes.rationale: Editors set the focal point so the important part stays visible across crop ratios.

nodes.label: Gallery/Album Features (future)
nodes.rationale: Albums by event/date, lightbox, lazy loading, optional download, EXIF stripped.

nodes.label: Image Categories and Aspect Ratios
nodes.rationale: Hero 16:9 1600x900, post/event thumbnails 16:10 800x500, gallery original max 1600px, profile 1:1 400x400, logos SVG.

nodes.label: Media Storage Layout
nodes.rationale: /public/media/ for Payload uploads, /public/images/ legacy pre-CMS files, sources outside the repo (DJI, phone); all images served from our own domain — no external CDNs for content photos.

nodes.label: Image Naming Convention
nodes.rationale: sprecher-east-{subject}-{context}-{year}.{ext}

nodes.label: Photo Optimization Rules
nodes.rationale: WebP preferred with JPEG fallback; 80-85% quality (90% for logos); max 200KB thumb / 500KB card / 1MB hero; sharp or imagemagick.

nodes.label: Media Size Variants (thumbnail 400x250, card 800x500)
nodes.rationale: Auto-generated on upload; alt text required; JPEG/PNG/WebP/GIF/SVG supported.

nodes.label: Accessibility Audit (axe-core / pa11y)
nodes.rationale: Contrast, alt text, labels, keyboard order, landmarks, skip link.

nodes.label: QA Tools and Commands
nodes.rationale: npx tsc --noEmit, pa11y, linkinator, lighthouse, npm audit --audit-level=high --omit=dev, npm run build.

nodes.label: Core Web Vitals Targets
nodes.rationale: LCP < 2.5s, INP <= 200ms, CLS < 0.1, Lighthouse 90+.

nodes.label: Image SEO
nodes.rationale: Descriptive filenames, contextual alt text, WebP with JPEG fallback, responsive srcset.

nodes.label: Efficiency Review Agent
nodes.rationale: Unnecessary work, missed concurrency, hot-path bloat, TOCTOU existence checks, memory leaks, overly broad reads.

nodes.label: Media Collection
nodes.rationale: Media uploads with size variants.

nodes.label: Media Manager Agent (media-mgr)
nodes.rationale: Every image must be high quality, optimized, attributed, accessible and self-hosted — no stock-photo feel; the site should look like a real neighborhood.

nodes.label: Ad-Hoc Work Tracking
nodes.rationale: All significant work, not just planned sprint items, must get an Asana task before the fix starts so the task board stays the source of truth.

nodes.label: Asana REST API via curl + PAT
nodes.norm_label: asana rest api via curl + pat
nodes.rationale: REST API chosen over the Asana MCP connector because the MCP lacks comment/story support, subtask creation, and has limited filtering; the PAT gives full API access.

nodes.label: /wrapped Post-Merge Checklist
nodes.rationale: Runs automatically when the user says PRs are merged: verify merge state with gh, complete Asana tasks from PR-body links, update MEMORY.md, sync main, report. Never assume state.

nodes.label: Asana Free Plan - Manual Linking
nodes.rationale: Asana free plan has no official GitHub app integration, so linking is manual (paste URLs both ways); a GitHub Action could automate it if the plan is upgraded.

nodes.label: One Task = One PR
nodes.rationale: Each task maps to exactly one PR for clean Asana-PR traceability, smaller focused diffs for review, and simpler rollback; Spike tasks are the exception.

nodes.label: Significance Threshold
nodes.rationale: Create a task when work yields a non-trivial commit, changes how agents work, or fixes something users notice; skip for typos, formatting-only, or work already covered by an open task.

nodes.label: Task Completion Rule
nodes.rationale: A task is only marked complete in Asana when its PR is merged to main; until then it stays open with progress comments so Asana remains an accurate record of what is actually in production.

nodes.label: Two-Way Task-PR Traceability
nodes.rationale: PR body carries the Asana URL and the Asana task carries the PR URL; this enables /wrapped to auto-complete tasks and makes navigation between project management and code trivial.

nodes.label: Windows JSON-via-temp-file Rule
nodes.rationale: Inline single-quoted JSON breaks in Git Bash on Windows, so payloads are written to temp files and passed with -d @file.

nodes.label: CMS Page Route Pattern ([slug]/page.tsx)
nodes.rationale: generateStaticParams + cached Page query + generateMetadata; React cache() deduplicates the fetch between Page and generateMetadata.

nodes.norm_label: layout builder blocks (archive, content, cta, formblock, mediablock, banner, code, relatedposts)

nodes.norm_label: cms hero types (highimpact, mediumimpact, lowimpact, none)

nodes.norm_label: lexical seed helpers (root, heading, p, text, linknode)

nodes.norm_label: reusable field helpers (link, linkgroup, defaultlexical, slug, hero)

nodes.rationale: Detail-page heroes are hardcoded per collection and deliberately not registered in the CMS hero selector.

nodes.rationale: A new block must be added both to the Pages layout blocks array and to the blockComponents map in RenderBlocks; missing either step silently fails and the block never renders.

nodes.label: SEO Plugin Type Gap
nodes.rationale: Plugins inject fields at runtime that generated types do not reflect, so safe type assertions with comments are used and the CollectionConfig generic is dropped when it conflicts.

nodes.label: Section Background Alternation
nodes.rationale: Consecutive sections must alternate bg-background and bg-surface to create visual rhythm.

nodes.label: Section Patterns (hero, stats strip, content, CTA banner)
nodes.norm_label: section patterns (hero, stats strip, content, cta banner)

nodes.label: Pattern Library Is a Floor, Not a Ceiling
nodes.norm_label: pattern library is a floor, not a ceiling
nodes.rationale: Patterns are proven starting points to combine and extend; values are minimalism with impact, purposeful asymmetry, smooth contextual flow, intuitiveness for laypeople, and elegance over flashiness.

nodes.label: Design Philosophy (3-second judgment)
nodes.rationale: Residents judge the site in 3 seconds; polish is the difference between a platform people use and one they ignore, so every page must look designed by a top-tier team.

nodes.label: Left-Align Content, Center Only Short Text
nodes.norm_label: left-align content, center only short text
nodes.rationale: Centering paragraph text is the hallmark of amateur design; professional layouts create visual balance through asymmetry (text left, visual right), not symmetry.

nodes.label: /simplify Skill (4 parallel review agents)
nodes.rationale: Runs code reuse, code quality, efficiency, and visual design review agents on the diff before a PR; the visual agent invokes /visual-design-review for frontend diffs.

nodes.label: WCAG AA Contrast Requirements (4.5:1 / 3:1)
nodes.rationale: Dark mode is not optional; every color combination is tested in both themes and invisible text is a critical bug.

nodes.label: Finding Format (severity, pattern, snippet, files)
nodes.rationale: If no existing pattern fits, the reviewer must write and test a new one in the pattern library before prescribing it, so the library grows with real fixes.

nodes.label: Review Priority Order (contrast first, motion last)
nodes.norm_label: review priority order (contrast first, motion last)

nodes.label: /visual-design-review Skill (design director)
nodes.rationale: Screenshots pages at 6 viewports and both themes, judges with principle-based taste, and prescribes brand-anchored fixes from the pattern library rather than redesigning from scratch.

nodes.label: Next.js 15 and Tailwind CSS v4 Patterns
nodes.norm_label: next.js 15 and tailwind css v4 patterns

nodes.label: Visual QA Is Mandatory for UI Changes
nodes.norm_label: visual qa is mandatory for ui changes
nodes.rationale: Code that builds but looks broken on mobile is a bug; the loop is change -> screenshot -> inspect -> fix -> re-screenshot -> commit at 6 viewports.

nodes.label: Styling Rules (no inline CSS, no hex colors)
nodes.norm_label: styling rules (no inline css, no hex colors)
nodes.rationale: All styling goes through Tailwind token classes so dark mode switches automatically and colors stay consistent across the site.

nodes.label: Root Layout title.template appends brand
nodes.rationale: The layout template '%s - Sprecher East' brands every title, so meta titles, generateMeta, and the SEO generateTitle must contain only the page name or the brand would be duplicated.

nodes.label: Design Token Discipline
nodes.rationale: Every fix references project tokens by name; hardcoded colors are allowed only for rgba scrims/shadows with no token equivalent.

nodes.label: Hexagonal Badge Emblem Design
nodes.description: Visual identity pattern used by the emblem: a hexagonal 'patch' shape containing a scenic illustration (sandstone bluffs, pines, river, curving road) with a green ribbon banner overlaid across the middle, interstate shields as the focal cluster, a tagline strip, and the agency seal as the signature, all set on a navy chevron-textured background.
nodes.rationale: The scenic bluffs-and-river illustration evokes the Wisconsin Dells / Baraboo Range landscape at the corridor's north end, tying the tourism pillar to place, while the interstate shields give instant route recognition; the badge format reads well at small sizes (it was downscaled to a 19 KB logo for the site).

nodes.label: I-39/90/94 Corridor Study

nodes.label: Housing Homes Backdrop Photo
nodes.description: Bright, real-estate-style exterior photo (1920px wide, landscape) of a white two-story timber house with a wraparound upper veranda, decorative lattice skirting, and a modern timber-clad single-story extension with large glass sliding doors. Foreground is a turquoise swimming pool with pale stone paving; palm trees, tropical potted plants, a lawn, and a clear blue sky frame the scene. Warm, sunny, aspirational mood. Architectural style is subtropical/coastal (Queenslander-like), not Midwestern suburban.

File name is fixed so a real neighborhood photo can replace it with no code change.

nodes.label: Secure Coding Rules
nodes.rationale: No eval/Function/dangerouslySetInnerHTML directly because input that seems trusted today can become untrusted as the codebase evolves; use safe wrappers such as JsonLd.

nodes.label: afterChange Revalidation Hook Pattern
nodes.rationale: Hooks accept and pass req, guard with context.disableRevalidate to prevent loops, and call revalidatePath/revalidateTag.

nodes.label: Documentation Is Code
nodes.rationale: Code snippets in rules and pattern libraries are templates developers adapt, so they must meet the same standards as production code.

nodes.label: Framework First
nodes.rationale: Use Payload/Next.js plugins and built-ins before custom code; a plugin is preferred even when custom looks simpler because it is maintained upstream.

nodes.label: Persist Before Side Effects
nodes.rationale: Side effects (email, external APIs) can fail and data loss is permanent, so the pattern is validate -> persist -> notify -> respond; Payload afterChange hooks enforce this naturally.

nodes.label: SOLID Principles (Payload flavored)
nodes.rationale: Single responsibility (handlers persist, hooks notify), open/closed via hooks and plugins, consistent data shapes, select/depth to limit props, depend on the Payload Local API rather than raw SQL.

nodes.label: Generic Auth Error Messages
nodes.rationale: Login, reset, and registration show fixed generic messages to prevent account enumeration and information leakage; raw errors are logged server-side only.

nodes.label: Four-Layer Dependency Security Guardrails
nodes.rationale: Agent rules at dev time, a pre-commit npm audit hook, a CI audit gate, and Dependabot together stop vulnerable dependencies at every stage.

nodes.label: Package Vetting Before Install
nodes.rationale: Prefer widely used (>1M weekly downloads), recently published packages and built-in Node/Next features; fewer deps means a smaller attack surface.

nodes.label: Scoped overrides for transitive vulnerabilities
nodes.rationale: Use package.json overrides scoped to the parent package rather than global overrides, and document them in the PR so reviewers understand the tradeoff.

nodes.label: npm weekly grouped updates
nodes.rationale: Patch updates and minor updates are each batched into one PR to reduce noise, while major versions get individual PRs because they may be breaking.

nodes.label: Wide Banner Crop (~4:1 Aspect Ratio)

nodes.label: Facebook-Sourced Photo (CDN Filename Pattern)
nodes.rationale: The filename shape 'NNNNNNNNN_NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN_NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN_n.jpg' is the naming convention Facebook's CDN assigns to downloaded photos, implying this image was pulled from the neighborhood's Facebook presence (community-contributed photo) rather than shot for the site or sourced from a stock provider. The opaque numeric name was kept as-is instead of being renamed to a descriptive backdrop file name.

nodes.label: Liatris (Blazing Star) prairie wildflower
nodes.description: Native Midwestern prairie perennial with tall purple flower spikes, a common pollinator plant in Wisconsin restored prairies and rain gardens; the dominant subject of the photo.

nodes.label: Instagram/Facebook CDN export filename pattern
nodes.description: The filename form <id>_<id>_<id>_n.jpg is the naming convention of images downloaded from Meta (Instagram/Facebook) CDNs, indicating this photo was pulled from a social post rather than produced in-house; provenance and reuse rights should be confirmed before publishing it on the site.

nodes.label: Native prairie planting / pollinator habitat
nodes.description: Theme depicted by the photo: a mixed native prairie planting (purple, white and yellow forbs plus grasses) typical of Madison-area parks, greenways and neighborhood pollinator gardens; aligns with the site's 'Parks & Recreation' and 'Property Values & Livability' content themes.

nodes.label: Prairie Wildflower Banner Photo (Blazing Star against blue sky)

Reads as a neighborhood greenspace / native pollinator garden photo. Not referenced anywhere in source code — an unused or manually placed asset in public/images.

nodes.label: CTA Volunteers Backdrop Photo

nodes.label: Get Involved / CTA Section Backdrop

Backdrops are rendered with next/image at very low opacity (about 0.06) under a tinted overlay, use object-cover, carry an empty alt attribute because they are decorative, and are downloaded at 1920px and compressed at quality 80 since sharpness is not needed at that opacity.

nodes.label: Placeholder Stock Backdrop (Unsplash)
nodes.rationale: Backdrop photos in public/images/backdrops are free stock placeholders (sourced from Unsplash, self-hosted to avoid external dependencies) used until real Sprecher East neighborhood photos are available. The stable file name cta-volunteers.jpg is deliberate so a real photo can replace it with no code changes. The depicted event is the Asian Para Games 2018 in Indonesia, not a Madison neighborhood scene, which is why it is treated as a temporary, low-opacity texture rather than an informational image.

nodes.label: Prairie Trail at Sunset (image-8.jpeg)
nodes.description: Landscape neighborhood photograph (2500x1875, 4:3). A mowed green grass walking path curves from the bottom-left foreground through a late-autumn restored prairie of tall dry golden grasses and fluffy seed heads. In the background sit white-sided two-story suburban homes with gabled roofs and porches, flanked by bare deciduous trees and evergreens. The sky is a dramatic golden-hour sunset: an orange-gold band at the horizon under a heavy purple-grey cloud layer. Reads as a park-edge greenway bordering a subdivision on Madison's far east side, likely used as a site hero or section backdrop image.

nodes.label: public-safety.jpeg — Nighttime suburban street with playground warning sign
nodes.description: Portrait-orientation neighborhood photo taken at dusk/night in late autumn. Middle: a straight concrete sidewalk with a grass terrace, young bare-branched street trees, and a quiet two-lane residential street lit by warm amber streetlights. Left: two-story suburban homes with lit porches and holiday-style lights. Right: open prairie/field edge. Sky: deep blue with a full moon crossed by an aircraft contrail. Mood is calm, safe, and well-lit — a walkable neighborhood at night. nodes.label: Legacy Squarespace UI Webfont Family
nodes.description: Multi-format icon webfont family (squarespace-ui-font.eot/.ttf/.woff/.svg) sitting in assets/fonts alongside self-hosted Poppins woff2 files.
nodes.rationale: Carried over from the pre-Next.js Squarespace export of the Sprecher East site so original assets are preserved in the repo. nodes.label: Squarespace UI Icon Font (SVG)
nodes.description: SVG-format icon webfont (font id 'squarespace-ui-font', 512 units-per-em, 16px icon grid) containing 54 monochrome UI glyphs mapped to Private Use Area codepoints (U+E000-U+E0xx plus FontAwesome-style U+F0xx). Glyphs are navigation/control icons: left/right/up/down chevrons and arrows, circled arrows, expand/collapse, and similar controls. Generated by IcoMoon. It is a legacy asset from the original Squarespace-hosted Sprecher East site and is not referenced anywhere in src/; the Next.js site uses Lucide React icons instead.

nodes.label: IcoMoon Icon Font Generator
